key.decision_why: The author answered the triager's feedback by posting screenshots and asking for another look, so the triager needs a short update. The PR's approach, file and commit are unchanged, so a new card is not warranted.
key.action_why: laurynmm reviewed the screenshots, judged the PR not on track to solve the issue, and closed it unmerged on 2026-10-06.
changed: The author posted two screenshots (a desktop-width one and a narrow one) in a PR comment.
The author says the 375px mobile view now keeps the email input and Change button inside the viewport.
No code was pushed: the head commit is the same as when the feedback was given.
still_missing: The PR description was not actually updated: it still says "Screenshots to be added by author in comments".
The screenshots are unlabeled 'after' images, not the precise before/after comparisons at several screen sizes that the issue requires.
Nothing shows the fix was checked against the reviewable-PR guide, and two self-review checklist items (strings/tooltips, corner cases) are still unchecked.
Another contributor's PR (#40052) for the same issue and the same file is still open, and this author never claimed the issue.
key.reply_ask: Ask the author to put labeled before/after screenshots at several narrow widths into the PR description, clearly showing the edit button fully visible and not overlapping the email input.

must_have.fact: Says there was no new push since the feedback: the code is unchanged and only screenshots were added in a comment.
Says the screenshots are not the labeled before/after comparisons at multiple screen sizes that issue #40051 requires, and that the description still has the screenshot placeholder.
Says the triager needs to inspect the screenshots to check that the edit button is really visible and doesn't overlap the input, before handing the PR off.
Mentions that PR #40052 by PrachiiiiisHere is another open attempt at the same issue touching web/styles/settings.css.
Does not recommend handing off to maintainer review: the next step is more feedback or closing.
